answer: Like a mesa rising above a flat desert, an agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake in escrow before it can transact. The stake is priced like saffron: affordable for one honest agent, but ruinous when multiplied across thousands of fake identities. Each verified transaction then grows a reputation plume that decays if the agent goes idle, so a sybil farmer cannot stockpile trust cheaply. If an agent is caught cheating, its stake is slashed and its plume collapses, turning every fake identity into a sunk cost rather than a free ticket.
